peers.scope: Exact vendor allocation-edit reversal and all eight implementation/factory variants; real padding/BOM/capacity admission and selected Node field loop; controls 1–12.
peers.finding: No concrete blocker in the assigned source slice; actual new-before-old-release and all original error/null checks are retained.

peers.scope: Native allocator TLS/prefix/rollback/lifetime; Parser/Config output ownership; Fixture/Budget/ConfigWorker/ParseWorker and controls 13–20; one-library build proposal.
peers.finding: No concrete blocker. Control 17 reaches actual retained partial implementation after larger allocation failure; control 18 warms parser capacity before field-copy failure. Native block entitlements survive parser/runtime release and thread cleanup joins before inspection.

ownership: Every real admitted parser allocation is reserved through the native memory owner before allocation. Replacement allocation and old allocation overlap are charged independently; no capacity-derived estimate substitutes for allocations.

The original vendor source and license are preserved unchanged. The separate owned copy contains only the enumerated allocator substitutions and private include, with exact full-byte reversion recorded.
Each allocated block retains its native memory owner in an aligned prefix. Parser and Config are independently owned, and Config bytes survive parser or runtime retirement.

The current raw C entry always leaves Config output null on failure and retires its temporary Config. An actual allocation failure makes the parser unusable until it is retired; the outer native binding must publish the actual failure before cleanup.
remaining_required_work: The actual Node GetPackageJSON invalid-config branch raises its native Error while the partial native Config is still alive. The next additive retained-invalid entry will preserve that lifetime for the JS binding, while retaining this raw entry's existing null-on-failure contract.
Physical ReadFileSync, actual native path and permission behavior, positive/negative cache publication, native error/JS serialization, and package-reader/Module assembly remain separate source units.
The ESM error-context Ada parse and native FileURLToPath dependency is not supplied by a legacy URL scanner.
No native compile, link, tests or original Node reference observations have been performed; this unit confers no complete loader or public namespace qualification.
